input.subject: meson's in-tree libpq header search order vs -Dextra_include_dirs

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at level 1a or 1b: the build failure is real and patch 1 makes meson match configure. Three fixable level 2 points remain. maintenance-fit-1 shows the CI canary does not cover include paths from pkg-config dependencies. maintenance-fit-2 and standards-compat-2 concern the optional libintl guess in patch 3 and the unstated back-patch scope, with the choice between v4 and the cppflags change still open.

brief.title: Meson: search in-tree libpq headers before external include directories
brief.problem: With meson and -Dextra_include_dirs, an installed older libpq-fe.h is found before the in-tree header, so the build fails (for example, unknown type PGcancelConn). configure/make puts the in-tree libpq directory first, so it is not affected. The author says this hits developers on macOS, the BSDs and some Linux distributions that install optional packages outside the default search paths.
brief.proposed_design: Patch 1 declares libpq as the first dependency in each meson.build that uses it, so libpq_inc comes before extra_include_dirs, c_flags and directories Meson finds. Patch 2 adds a CI check that puts a canary libpq-fe.h with #error into the include path, for both meson and configure. Patches 3 and 4 find libintl from the msgfmt prefix and drop -Dextra_XXX from the FreeBSD and macOS CI tasks.
user_visible_surface: Changed meaning of meson option -Dextra_include_dirs: its directories now come after the in-tree libpq headers.
New libintl discovery in meson (patch 3) that guesses the prefix from the location of msgfmt in $PATH.
author_claims: The fix is mostly a mechanical reorder of dependency lists and makes meson match the configure build.
Any non-Linux system with an installed libpq-with-headers package could hit the failure; the author may be the only one affected so far.
The fix should be back-patched to 16, where meson arrived.
With patch 3, FreeBSD and macOS with MacPorts build without -Dextra_XXX, and all CI operating systems pass.
Removing the catch-all include path exposed missing dependency declarations, such as gssapi for libpq_oauth_st.
brief.thread_state: Heikki does not object but fears the order rule will break again; Tristan calls patch 1 ready and doubts patch 3. Andres proposed moving extra_include_dirs into cppflags, and Thomas answered that paths from other dependencies can still expose an external libpq-fe.h, so the approach is still open.
unclear: The material does not say which approach the author wants to commit: v4 reordering or Andres's cppflags change.
No current, rebased patch is visible; CFbot asked for a rebase in November 2025.
The material does not say if patches 3 and 4 are meant for back-patching or only for master.
Patch 3 assumes the library directory is named "lib"; the material gives no answer to Tristan on multilib layouts.
The material does not show a fix for the Windows ordering problem Andres raised, with extra_include_dirs placed before src/include/port/win32.

prior_attempts.title: Allow meson to find ICU in non-standard location
prior_attempts.quote: Obviously we'd like a little better solution so that others don't get confused, but it's not really a problem for me any more.
prior_attempts.reason: The author withdrew it because setting -Dextra_lib_dirs, as Jacob Champion suggested, already worked with ICU 72 without the patch. Andres Freund had also pointed to -Dpkg_config_path, which finds ICU but did not add the RPATH in the author's test. The author said a clearer solution or doc updates would still help others.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P5 changed how meson finds ICU when -Dextra_* options are given, and its author withdrew it because his own case already worked. Patch 3 here guesses the libintl prefix from msgfmt so that no -Dextra_* option is needed; patches 1 and 2 fix header order, which P5 did not touch.

objections.title: Order convention in about 30 meson.build files has only partial CI coverage
objections.failure_scenario: A later patch adds a frontend tool with `dependencies: [libxml, libpq]`. On FreeBSD, pkg-config for libxml adds -I/usr/local/include, where a packaged older libpq-fe.h lives. CI stays green because the canary sits only in -Dextra_include_dirs, and a developer finds out when their own build fails.
objections.argument: Patch 1 makes correctness depend on list order in about 30 build files, which message #9 calls a "flimsy list that is copied all over the place". Heikki's concern in message #6 is met by patch 2, but only for paths from extra_include_dirs and --with-includes. Message #16 says paths from other dependencies can expose an external libpq-fe.h again. The canary does not cover that source.
objections.author_must_show: Can the canary check also cover include paths from pkg-config dependencies, or can the ordering be set in one central place so new meson.build files cannot get it wrong?

critic.reasoning: Message #16 itself says paths from other dependencies can expose an external libpq-fe.h. The canary in patch 2 sits only under --with-includes and -Dextra_include_dirs, so a wrong order next to a pkg-config dependency passes CI.

objections.title: Guessing the libintl prefix from msgfmt is a heuristic core must keep
objections.failure_scenario: A macOS user has Homebrew and MacPorts, and the msgfmt first in $PATH comes from the other prefix or from a multilib layout using lib64. Meson then takes libintl headers or libraries from a prefix the user did not choose. The user may not see the mismatch until link time or run time.
objections.argument: Patch 3 itself asks whether there is a reason not to do this. Tristan objects to the hard-coded "lib" directory in message #14, and the thread does not answer him. Once released, users will depend on this discovery rule, and every later packaging layout becomes a report against core. Patch 3 is not needed for the libpq fix, and the material does not say whether it would be back-patched.
objections.author_must_show: Can patches 3 and 4 move to a separate master-only thread, and what does the probe do when msgfmt and libintl come from different prefixes or use lib64?

critic.reasoning: The author's reply in message #12 covers a guess that finds nothing, but not a guess that finds a libintl in a prefix the user did not choose. Tristan's point about the hardcoded "lib" has no answer in the thread.

objections.title: Back-patch scope does not say which patches go to stable branches
objections.failure_scenario: A distribution rebuilds a 16.x minor release with its existing meson options. If patch 3 is back-patched, which libintl Meson finds can change within the minor release. A Windows packager may also see a different header order if Andres's cppflags approach replaces v4.
objections.argument: Message #9 and the v4-0001 commit message plan a back-patch to 16. Only patch 1 is a plain reorder; patch 3 changes how a dependency is found. Message #16 leaves open whether v4 or the cppflags change will be committed, and that choice decides what packagers of stable branches see.
objections.author_must_show: Which of the four patches, and which of the two approaches, is meant for 16 through 19, and which only for master?

critic.reasoning: Only v4-0001 says "Back-patch to 16", and message #9 planned patches 1 and 2 for 16+. The thread leaves open the choice between v4 and the cppflags change, and that choice decides header order in stable branches.

refuted.title: Libintl guess from msgfmt prefix adds a heuristic where an option already works
refuted.failure_scenario: A developer on a multilib or mixed-prefix system has msgfmt in one prefix and the wanted libintl elsewhere, or under lib64. Patch 3 guesses "<prefix>/lib" and picks a libintl that does not match the expected headers, or fails to find one. The developer learns this at build or link time, with no clear message that a guess was made.
refuted.argument: Patch 3 targets a case that -Dextra_include_dirs and -Dextra_lib_dirs already handle, which is how [P5] ended: a meson discovery change for a library in a non-standard location was withdrawn once the existing options were shown to work. Tristan's concern in message #14 about hardcoding "lib" got no reply. In message #16 the author also notes that libintl paths found this way can expose an external libpq-fe.h again. The commit message itself asks whether this is a bad idea.
refuted.author_must_show: How does patch 3 behave on lib64 or multilib layouts, and should it stay out of the back-patch to 16 and ship only in master?

precedents.title: Allow meson to find ICU in non-standard location

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-2. P5 must not be used as support: its author withdrew it because his own case already worked, which is not a ruling against discovery heuristics.

refuted.title: Libintl prefix guessed from msgfmt in PATH can pick the wrong library
refuted.failure_scenario: A macOS packager has both Homebrew and MacPorts installed, and msgfmt from one comes first in $PATH. Meson then links libintl and its headers from that prefix, while pkg-config finds the other libraries in the other prefix. On a multilib system the guessed "lib" directory may hold the wrong architecture. The packager finds out at link time, at run time, or when users report it.
refuted.argument: Today a missing libintl stops the build and asks for -Dextra_XXX; with patch 3, Meson quietly takes a guessed prefix. The commit message asks whether there is a reason not to do this, and Tristan's point about the hardcoded "lib" got no answer (message #14). In message #16 the author notes that dependency paths found this way can bring an external libpq-fe.h back into view, so the guess also reopens the bug that patch 1 fixes. No other Meson dependency in the tree is found this way.
refuted.author_must_show: When the guessed prefix differs from where pkg-config found the other libraries, or the layout uses lib64, what does Meson do, and does the configure log say so?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-2. It also misreads message #16: the libintl path exposes an external libpq-fe.h again under the cppflags approach, while patch 1 puts libpq first to cover dependency paths.

refuted.title: Patch 3 adds a guessing path where -Dextra_XXX already works
refuted.failure_scenario: A MacPorts or FreeBSD user has msgfmt in $PATH from one prefix and libintl in a lib64 or multilib directory elsewhere. Meson guesses the msgfmt prefix and builds against a different libintl than intended. The user finds out only when NLS fails at link or run time, with no -Dextra_XXX on the command line to explain it.
refuted.argument: -Dextra_include_dirs and -Dextra_lib_dirs already find libintl on these systems, and CI uses them today (message #12, patch 4). Patch 3 makes this more convenient but adds a second discovery mechanism, and its commit message asks whether this is a bad idea. Tristan questions the hardcoded "lib" (message #14), and Thomas notes that dependency-supplied paths like this one can expose an external libpq-fe.h again (message #16). The author's answer, "No loss if it guesses wrong" (message #12), covers a failed guess but not a wrong guess that still compiles.
refuted.author_must_show: What does the msgfmt-prefix guess give that the existing -Dextra_XXX options do not, and how is a wrong but compiling guess detected?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-2, which states the same wrong-guess case and the same open question from message #14.

refuted.title: Libintl guessing from msgfmt location has no stated user demand
refuted.failure_scenario: A developer on a multilib or custom-prefix system runs meson without -Dextra_XXX. Patch 3 then probes `<prefix>/lib` next to msgfmt and links a libintl the user did not choose. The user finds out at link time or run time, and back-branch maintainers carry the heuristic.
refuted.argument: Patch 3 does not fix the reported bug. It removes the need for -Dextra_XXX, which works today and which Tom says exists because BSD-derived platforms need it (message #11). No user in the thread asks for automatic libintl discovery. The author calls it experimental (message #12) and its commit message asks whether there is a reason not to do this. Tristan doubts the hardcoded "lib" directory (message #14), and that point has no answer.
refuted.author_must_show: Which users or packagers have asked to build without -Dextra_XXX, and why is the current option not enough for them?

critic.reasoning: Messages #11 and #12 show the need is common: builds on BSD-derived systems and macOS need -Dextra_XXX today, and with NLS only for libintl. The remaining concern about the heuristic is covered by maintenance-fit-2.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: Patch 1 says "Back-patch to 16"; the scope for patches 3 and 4 is not stated.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Patch 1 sets a dependency order rule in about 30 meson.build files, and patch 3 adds a libintl discovery heuristic.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Which approach is proposed for commit: the v4 reorder of dependency lists, or the move of extra_include_dirs into cppflags from message #15?
Which of the four patches go to branches 16 and later, and which are for master only?
Can the canary check also cover include paths that come from pkg-config dependencies, so a wrong order next to such a dependency fails CI?
What does patch 3 do when msgfmt and libintl are in different prefixes, or when the library directory is lib64?
Does the chosen approach fix the Windows case from message #15, where extra_include_dirs comes before src/include/port/win32?

committability.owner_note: The CommitFest entry lists Thomas Munro as author, and the brief reports Heikki and Andres in the thread. The owner needs to know the meson build and the CI setup.
committability.liability: The owner signs for include order in about 30 meson.build files on branches 16 and later, and for any later file that gets the order wrong. If patch 3 goes in, the owner also answers reports about libintl found in an unexpected prefix.
committability.author_follow_up: The author carries the patch in all his development branches (message #3) and posted four versions. CFbot asked for a rebase in November 2025 and no rebased patch is visible.

priority.reason: The failure hits developers who build with meson while an older libpq package with headers is installed outside the default paths. Patch 1 is a mechanical reorder, but the thread has not settled between v4 and the cppflags change, and patch 3 is separable from the fix.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so this review cannot confirm that every target that includes libpq-fe.h gets libpq first, or what patch 3 probes. Only 3 of 16 messages were visible; later messages are known from the brief and the objections.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improvements to Meson docs
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch series adds and reorganizes the installation documentation for building Postgres with meson. Follow-up patches fix meson docs errors, add a data layout options sub-section, remove the Anti-Features section, reorder the Miscellaneous section and rewrite the short version of the install guide.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author stopped responding. Andres Freund (section order, merging the Anti-Features options) and Tristan Partin (meson compile instead of ninja, directory layout for the short version) left review comments that got no follow-up for months, so the entry was returned with feedback. The initial documentation had already been committed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I have changed the status of commitfest entry to "Returned with
Feedback" as there was no followup on Tristan Partin and Andres's
comments from many months.

precedents_retrieved.title: Meson build updates
precedents_retrieved.summary: A set of small cleanups to the Meson build, mostly for consistency with surrounding code. The larger changes added Meson overrides for binaries and libpq and removed the Meson program options for specifying tool paths in favor of machine files.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund rejected removing the program path options because Meson machine files cannot be changed without a new build directory and are hard to use from the command line. He also found overrides for every binary not worth the extra boilerplate, so the author cut that patch down to libpq. Some patches were pushed in July 2023. The last message asks about the pending pkg-config(python3) patch with no visible reply, and the messages do not show why the entry was withdrawn.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: So I really don't want to remove these options.

precedents_retrieved.title: Speed up clean meson builds by ~25%
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Tom Lane, Peter Eisentraut, Robert Haas
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch moves the build of the generated ecpg preproc file near the top of the meson build order, so its long compile overlaps with other files. The author reported clean builds dropping from about 40 to about 30 seconds on a clang build.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane planned an ecpg grammar fix for v18 that removes the slow compile, and did not want to change the build rules for a temporary problem. Retests showed small gains: Peter Eisentraut measured 1% slower with gcc-14 and 3% faster with clang-18, and Robert Haas saved about 3 seconds. Robert Haas concluded that the patch helps only back-branch builds using clang without ccache and an older ninja, which is too narrow to justify it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think
that's a small enough savings with enough conditionals that we should
not bother.

precedents_retrieved.title: Invalid postgres version detection in meson.build
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes the devel check in meson.build from pg_version.endswith('devel') to pg_version.contains('devel'), to match the beta and rc checks. The author considered the current check a bug in version detection.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Heikki Linnakangas replied that the current code is correct. Beta and rc version strings end with a number, such as "17beta1" or "16rc2", but devel version strings never do, such as "17devel", so endswith('devel') is enough.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I believe it's correct as it is.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow meson to find ICU in non-standard location
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes meson so that it finds ICU in a non-standard location when -Dextra_lib_dirs and -Dextra_include_dirs are given, by searching for the library directly. The author was unsure about the approach, partly because meson then reports only "YES" and not the ICU version found.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew it because setting -Dextra_lib_dirs, as Jacob Champion suggested, already worked with ICU 72 without the patch. Andres Freund had also pointed to -Dpkg_config_path, which finds ICU but did not add the RPATH in the author's test. The author said a clearer solution or doc updates would still help others.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Obviously we'd like a little better solution so that others don't get
confused, but it's not really a problem for me any more.

precedents_retrieved.title: preserve timestamps when installing headers
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds `-p` to the `cp` calls in `src/include/Makefile` so installed headers keep their modification times. Together with `INSTALL="install -p"` passed to configure, this would stop `make install` from forcing a rebuild of extensions that depend on the headers.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane pointed out that POSIX `cp -p` also preserves file ownership, which breaks the usual case of building as a normal user and installing as root. He and Peter Eisentraut also doubted the benefit was worth a change to the build rules, since ccache covers rebuild cost and build systems rarely track timestamps outside the tree. Discussion moved to switching header installation back to `$(INSTALL)` with user-supplied switches, but no revised patch appears in the thread.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It also specifies preserving file ownership,
which seems absolutely catastrophic for the standard use-case of
"build as some ordinary user, then install as root".

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow COPY "text" to output a header and add header matching mode to COPY FROM
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets COPY write and read a HEADER line in the text format, which before was allowed only in CSV mode. A later version also adds HEADER match to COPY FROM, which requires the header line to match the target column names in both text and CSV format.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier returned the patch with feedback after the v5 revision. He judged it wrong to treat HEADER as a boolean-like option with one extra "match" value, and suggested a separate option for clear semantics. He also asked that repeated HEADER options be detected as redundant, as COPY does for "format". The first 2018 version was returned earlier because his review, which also raised header matching, was not addressed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It seems to me that we may
actually be looking at having this stuff as an option different than
"header" at the end to have clear semantics.

precedents_retrieved.title: Create shorthand for including all extra tests
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds an 'all' value for PG_TEST_EXTRA, checked through a new check_extra_tests_enabled() function in Test/Utils.pm, so a full run includes every extra test suite. After feedback it replaced 'all' with a 'needs-private-lo' category that enables the kerberos, ldap, load_balance and ssl tests.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the extra tests are excluded by default because they are security hazards, so each should be reviewed before it is enabled. Peter Eisentraut said 'needs-private-lo' is not the only condition, since kerberos and ldap need extra software and load_balance may need edits to the hosts file. He also preferred each test deciding on its own over a central mapping, and saw no sensible grouping for six values. The author agreed to revisit the idea if more PG_TEST_EXTRA options appear.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
So someone would still need to familiarize themselves with these tests
individually before setting a global option like this.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Optimize order of GROUP BY keys".
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Optimize order of GROUP BY keys".
Reverted commit(s): Optimize order of GROUP BY keys
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit db0d67db2401eb6238ccc04c6407a4fd4f985832 and
several follow-on fixes.  The idea of making a cost-based choice
of the order of the sorting columns is not fundamentally unsound,
but it requires cost information and data statistics that we don't
really have.  For example, relying on procost to distinguish the
relative costs of different sort comparators is pretty pointless
so long as most such comparator functions are labeled with cost 1.0.
Moreover, estimating the number of comparisons done by Quicksort
requires more than just an estimate of the number of distinct values
in the input: you also need some idea of the sizes of the larger
groups, if you want an estimate that's good to better than a factor of
three or so.  That's data that's often unknown or not very reliable.
Worse, to arrive at estimates of the number of calls made to the
lower-order-column comparison functions, the code needs to make
estimates of the numbers of distinct values of multiple columns,
which are necessarily even less trustworthy than per-column stats.
Even if all the inputs are perfectly reliable, the cost algorithm
as-implemented cannot offer useful information about how to order
sorting columns beyond the point at which the average group size
is estimated to drop to 1.

Close inspection of the code added by db0d67db2 shows that there
are also multiple small bugs.  These could have been fixed, but
there's not much point if we don't trust the estimates to be
accurate in-principle.

Finally, the changes in cost_sort's behavior made for very large
changes (often a factor of 2 or so) in the cost estimates for all
sorting operations, not only those for multi-column GROUP BY.
That naturally changes plan choices in many situations, and there's
precious little evidence to show that the changes are for the better.
Given the above doubts about whether the new estimates are really
trustworthy, it's hard to summon much confidence that these changes
are better on the average.

Since we're hard up against the release deadline for v15, let's
revert these changes for now.  We can always try again later.

Note: in v15, I left T_PathKeyInfo in place in nodes.h even though
it's unreferenced.  Removing it would be an ABI break, and it seems
a bit late in the release cycle for that.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Blind attempt to fix _configthreadlocale() failures on MinGW."
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Blind attempt to fix _configthreadlocale() failures on MinGW."
Reverted commit(s): Blind attempt to fix _configthreadlocale() failures on MinGW.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 2cf91ccb73ce888c44e3751548fb7c77e87335f2.

When using the old msvcrt.dll, MinGW would supply its own dummy version
of _configthreadlocale() that just returns -1 if you try to use it.  For
a time we tolerated that to shut the build farm up.  We would fall back
to code that was enough for the tests to pass, but it would surely have
risked crashing a real multithreaded program.

We don't need that kludge anymore, because we can count on ucrt.  We
expect the real _configthreadlocale() to be present, and the ECPG tests
will now fail if it isn't.  The workaround was dead code and it's time
to revert it.

(A later patch still under review proposes to remove this use of
_configthreadlocale() completely but we're unwinding this code in
steps.)

roaster_notes.note: No prior attempt matches patches 1-2, the libpq header order fix and the CI canary. The thread treats them as a parity fix with configure, so this angle raises nothing against them.
Patch 1 brings meson in line with configure and changes no SQL, GUC, pg_dump or psql surface. On the main fix, this angle has no objection.

The proposal changes only meson build scripts and CI configuration, so it has no on-disk, WAL, replication, catalog or wire protocol state. The one related point is that pg_config --cppflags may gain extra include dirs under Andres's variant, which affects extension builds only and is outside this angle.

The proposal changes the build system only: include path order in meson, a CI canary header, and libintl discovery at build time. It adds no runtime privilege, role, setting or data path. Who runs the build already controls every include path, so no new trust boundary appears. Patch 3 guesses the libintl prefix from msgfmt in $PATH, and $PATH is the builder's own environment.
The libpq reorder itself is a bug fix that matches configure, and Heikki and Tristan support it. The objections above are about how long the fix lasts and about the optional patch 3.
Patch 1 fixes a build-order bug whose only workaround is uninstalling libpq, and message #11 discussed CFLAGS and set it aside. Only the optional patch 3 is open to a convenience objection.
Patch 1 and its CI check fix a real build failure and match configure behaviour. Tom confirms that BSD-derived platforms need the include option, so a demand objection to them would not hold.
